proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If \(U=\varnothing\) and \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\ne\varnothing\), then \(q\) is identified if and only if no exact support \(S\) realized by a member of \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) admits a fully observed completion obstruction. Agreement yields a support-valid guarded g-formula. If a realized exact support \(S\) admits a completion obstruction, then for every integer \(r\geq 3\) there exist compatible rational models \(M_1^{(r)},M_2^{(r)}\) with identical observed laws and exact support \(S\) such that \(\lvert q(M_1^{(r)})-q(M_2^{(r)})\rvert\geq 1-2/r>0\). For this existentially constructed pair, every primitive observed-node conditional-table probability is encoded separately as a reduced fraction with denominator at most \(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), and its numerator-denominator pair has length at most \(2\lceil\log_2(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|)\rceil+2\) bits. No common denominator is required, and induced cells are exact sum-product evaluations of those fractions. These witnesses existentially select a common observational fiber for each obstruction; the theorem does not claim the same gap on every fixed same-support observational law. Taking \(r=8\) gives a \(3/4\)-gap witness with denominator bound \(8|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), and the certified gap approaches one at an additional \(O(\log r)\) primitive-bit cost.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The established smoothing proof is parameterized by every integer \(r\geq3\), whereas the frozen public statement still records only an instance-dependent positive gap and the \(r=8\) arithmetic bound. The proposed text states the proved quantifiers and bounds and makes explicit that the construction chooses a common observational fiber rather than controlling every fixed law on the support.
